subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity increase + burst provisioning options
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlasai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+procurement@atlasai.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation + capacity ask for Q3

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. As we approach our renewal (end of June), our infra team has done a forecast and we need to discuss a material increase to our dedicated pool. High level: we expect production traffic to grow ~3x over the next 6-9 months.

Ask: can Redwood support adding ~40 dedicated GPUs to our reserved pool as part of the renewal, and what are the options for handling short-term traffic spikes? Specifically:
- Do you offer on-demand spillover to hosted capacity when reserved is saturated?
- If yes, what are the pricing and expected impact on latency/throughput?
- If not, can we set a hard cap with guaranteed throttling behavior and SLA implications?

We have an internal throughput SLO target of 2500 seq/sec (seq len 128) at p95 latency <= 200ms for inference routes serving interactive traffic. Any guarantees you'll commit to are helpful for our procurement team.

I've attached a short deck with traffic projections and peak-day profiles (Atlas_Request_0615.pdf). Can we get a proposal by EOD Thursday (18 Jun)? We prefer a model that gives predictable spend but still allows short bursts without manual escalation.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure
Atlas AI

---
Attachment: Atlas_Request_0615.pdf (3 pages)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlasai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 12:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity ask for Q3

Hi Marta — great to hear from you and thanks for the projection deck. We can absolutely support a larger reserved pool and have three pragmatic patterns customers choose between for burst handling. Below is a concise summary so your procurement and infra teams can weigh tradeoffs; Ben and Dylan are looped in for pricing and infra details.

Option A — Strict reserved-only (hard cap)
- Add 40 reserved GPUs into a dedicated pool. No automatic spillover; requests beyond reserved capacity are queued/throttled.
- Guarantees: 99.9% availability for reserved capacity; latency SLOs apply only to requests served from reserved pool.
- Simpler procurement; predictable monthly commit, but spikes may be rate-limited.

Option B — Soft-reserve + on-demand spillover (recommended for interactive workloads)
- Reserved pool (baseline) + automatic spillover to hosted on-demand when reserved capacity is saturated.
- We propose a pre-funded burst credit bucket to cover short spikes (configurable, e.g., 25% of monthly token budget) for the first 90 days of the amendment, then transition to pay-as-you-go for overage.
- Impact: spillover routing may add ~20–40% p95 latency increase depending on model/region; we can limit spillover by route.
- Guarantees: throughput SLA applies to reserved pool; we provide throughput guidance for spillover but cannot promise identical latency SLA for on-demand.

Option C — Reserved + ephemeral hot standby (buffered reserved capacity)
- Add a small ephemeral reserved buffer (hot standby GPUs) that are billed at a reduced reserved rate for a limited time-window to cover bursts.
- Predictable billing and lower latency than on-demand but higher committed cost than soft-reserve.

We can draft amendment language that includes preferred option, burst-credit sizing, and the SLA carve-outs for spillover. Ben — can you confirm pricing deltas for on-demand token rates and recommended burst-credit size? Dylan — can you confirm expected latency uplift for a typical seq=128 interactive model when spilled to hosted on-demand instances?

I can draft a redline for the amendment if Atlas picks an option. We can target finalizing paperwork by 30 Jun if that aligns with your procurement timeline.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity ask for Q3

Stephanie / team — engineering take below. I pulled numbers from our capacity model and ran a quick sim against Atlas's peak profile. See attached cost model for the math (capacity_cost_model_q3.xlsx).

Key confirmations and recommendations:
- Adding 40x A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool covers baseline 3x growth with ~15% headroom for sustained traffic.
- Throughput guidance: for seq=128 interactive models we estimate ~2300–2800 seq/s aggregate depending on model family and batching efficiency; p95 latency target of <=200ms is achievable on reserved hardware with proper batching and cache warming.
- Spillover behavior: when reserved pool is saturated, requests are routed to our hosted fleet in the same region. Expected p95 latency uplift ~25–35% (model dependent). We observed up to 60–80ms additional latency in our sim for GPT-style workloads.
- Suggested burst policy for renewal: 1) 90-day promo credit that covers up to 25% of typical monthly token usage for spillover (absorbed from prepaid bucket), 2) after promo, overage billed at hosted on-demand rates (list below).
- Failover controls: per-route caps, sticky routing (prefer reserved until KV cache warms on-hosted), and emergency hard cap toggle (customer or Redwood triggered) for noisy neighbors.

Proposed billing primitives (examples):
- Reserved gpu add-on: $X,XXX / GPU / month (commit price)
- On-demand token rate (spillover): $0.000Y / token beyond credit bucket
- Prepaid burst credit: one-time allocation tied to the amendment period

Next steps: Stephanie to propose which option Atlas prefers and we will produce an amendment + SOW that includes the 90-day promo. Laura — please prep the SOW template and include the exact SLA carve-outs for spillover.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Infra Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_cost_model_q3.xlsx (spreadsheet with sims)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlasai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ops+procurement@atlasai.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed amendment: Reserved + burst credits (90-day promo) — Redwood x Atlas

Hi Marta — thanks for the quick turn. Based on your deck and the engineering confirmation below, we recommend Option B (Soft-reserve + on-demand spillover) as the best balance between predictable commit and spike resiliency.

Summary of proposed amendment (high level):
- Add 40x A100-equivalent GPUs to Atlas's dedicated reserved pool, effective on renewal (amendment start date: 2026-07-01).
- 90-day promotional burst credit bucket sized at 25% of Atlas's average monthly token consumption (one-time allocation) to cover automatic on-demand spillover.
- After the 90-day promo, spillover is billed at on-demand token rates. We will include per-route caps and a customer-controlled emergency hard cap toggle in the Console.
- SLAs: Throughput and latency guarantees apply to reserved capacity (99.9% availability; p95 latency target <=200ms at seq=128). Spillover routes are best-effort; we will provide guidance and historical metrics but cannot guarantee identical latency.

Attachments for review: Redwood_Dedicated_Amendment_v1.docx, SOW_Redwood-Atlas_v3.pdf (pricing and implementation timeline included). If this matches your expectations, I'll send a DocuSign package and the redline for the amendment.

DocuSign (preview): https://docusign.com/xyz/Redwood-Atlas-Amendment
Next steps: confirm acceptance of the 90-day promo and preferred billing treatment (prepaid credit vs monthly netting) by 24 Jun; final sign by 30 Jun to meet provisioning lead times.

Thanks and happy to jump on a short call to walk through.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
